# The coupled algorithm and its mean field {#sec-algorithm}

## State space and MCMC transition

Fix $\pi$ on $\mathbb R^d$, with finite mean $m$ and strictly positive-definite covariance $C$.  Let

$$
\Theta=\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb S_{++}^d
             \times\mathrm{St}(d,r),\qquad
\theta=(\mu,\Gamma,W).
$$ {#eq-theta-domain}

For definiteness, $P_\Gamma$ is the symmetric random-walk Metropolis kernel targeting $\pi$, with proposal $Y=x+\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon\sim N(0,\ell^2\Gamma)$, for fixed $\ell>0$.  In particular $P_\theta=P_\Gamma$ does not depend on $\mu$ or $W$, and

$$
\pi P_\Gamma=\pi,\qquad \Gamma\in\mathbb S_{++}^d.
$$ {#eq-common-invariant}

A possible implementation may allow further dependence on $W$, but that would require a separate kernel-regularity verification.  We do not assume it here.

## Sample-driven Oja iteration

Define the horizontal Oja increment

$$
G(\mu,W,x)
=(I-WW^\top)(x-\mu)(x-\mu)^\top W.
$$ {#eq-oja-observable}

Since $W^\top G(\mu,W,x)=0$, this is tangent to the Stiefel manifold.  We use the polar retraction

$$
R_W(U)=(W+U)(I_r+U^\top U)^{-1/2},
\qquad W^\top U=0.
$$ {#eq-polar-retraction}

::: {#def-coupled-recursion}
## Coupled adaptive Markov--Oja recursion

Given $X_n,\mu_n,\Gamma_n,W_n$ with $\Gamma_n\succ0$ and $W_n^\top W_n=I_r$, draw $X_{n+1}\sim P_{\Gamma_n}(X_n,\cdot)$ and update

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mu_{n+1}
 &=\mu_n+\gamma_{n+1}(X_{n+1}-\mu_n),\\
\Gamma_{n+1}
 &=\Gamma_n+\gamma_{n+1}\big[
    (X_{n+1}-\mu_n)(X_{n+1}-\mu_n)^\top-\Gamma_n\big],\\
W_{n+1}
 &=R_{W_n}\!\left(\gamma_{n+1}G(\mu_n,W_n,X_{n+1})\right).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-coupled-algorithm}

We take $0<\gamma_n<1$ to preserve $\Gamma_n\succ0$ by convexity.
:::

The first two lines are the mean--covariance adaptation of @andrieuMoulines2006, equations (4)--(6).  The third line is an additional Oja estimator based on the *same* accepted states.  There is no independently simulated PCA data stream.

## Averaging over the common invariant distribution

For $z=x-\mu$, define the ambient observable

$$
H(\theta,x)=
\begin{pmatrix}
x-\mu\\
(x-\mu)(x-\mu)^\top-\Gamma\\
G(\mu,W,x)
\end{pmatrix}.
$$ {#eq-ambient-observable}

The identity $x-\mu=(x-m)-( \mu-m)$, followed by expansion of the outer product, gives

$$
\pi\big[(x-\mu)(x-\mu)^\top\big]
=C+(\mu-m)(\mu-m)^\top
=Q(\mu).
$$ {#eq-second-moment-identity}

The mixed terms vanish because $\pi(x-m)=0$.  Therefore

$$
h(\theta)=\pi[H(\theta,\cdot)]
=
\begin{pmatrix}
m-\mu\\
Q(\mu)-\Gamma\\
(I-WW^\top)Q(\mu)W
\end{pmatrix}.
$$ {#eq-coupled-field}

This averaged field is the same algebraically whether the innovations are independent with law $\pi$ or are generated by the changing kernels $P_{\Gamma_n}$.  What changes is the justification of replacing path averages by $\pi$-averages.

The limiting ODE is consequently

$$
\dot\mu=m-\mu,\quad
\dot\Gamma=Q(\mu)-\Gamma,\quad
\dot W=(I-WW^\top)Q(\mu)W.
$$ {#eq-coupled-ode}

The $W$-field is horizontal: $W^\top\dot W=0$, hence
$\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}(W^\top W)=0$ for the embedded-space ODE.  The Stiefel manifold is invariant under its flow.  The covariance-driven variant $\dot W=(I-WW^\top)\Gamma W$ is a **different algorithm** and is not used in the main theorem.
